_note: B-62. DeviceOps write levers (PowerShell, offline mock RMM device state; no RMM is called). Each runs one vetted script from levers/powershell/DeviceOps/vetted-scripts.json; there is no script, path or command parameter. reboot carries window business-hours and reboot-server window maintenance; the runner (B-42) applies the window, the lever holds no time logic. All field shapes are UNVERIFIED stand-ins; see levers/powershell/DeviceOps/SOURCES.md.

levers.name: device.restart-spooler
levers.description: Restart the Print Spooler on one device of the client and clear its stuck print jobs, using the vetted script dev-spooler-restart. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

impact.L1: Printing works again for the person at that desk; the stuck jobs are removed, so they print them again.
impact.L2: A front desk or office that cannot print is back to work without a remote session.
impact.L3: A request technicians handle many times a week becomes one approved, audited step.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.

levers.name: device.repair-mapped-drive
levers.description: Reconnect one mapped network drive letter on one device of the client, using the vetted script dev-drive-repair. The share path is the one already saved on the device. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

drive.description: Drive letter D to Z that is already mapped on the device

impact.L1: The person gets their shared files back; a drive letter that does not exist on the device is refused.
impact.L2: The office keeps working from its file share instead of waiting for a remote session.
impact.L3: One of the most common Tier 1 fixes becomes a named, approved and audited step.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.

levers.name: device.reset-outlook-profile
levers.description: Rename one user's Outlook profile data on one device to a dated backup so a new profile is built, using the vetted script dev-outlook-reset. Mail on the server is not touched. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

user.description: Windows account name whose Outlook profile is reset, as listed on the device

impact.L1: The person's Outlook opens again with a new profile; cached data is rebuilt, so the first start is slow.
impact.L2: A mailbox that will not open stops blocking a person's day; the old profile data is kept under a dated name.
impact.L3: A fix that took a remote session and a risky manual rename becomes an approved step with a rollback note.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.

levers.name: device.cleanup-temp
levers.description: Move temp files older than 7 days on one device into a dated quarantine folder, using the vetted script dev-temp-cleanup. Nothing is deleted. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

impact.L1: The device frees disk space and runs better; nothing is deleted, the old files wait in a quarantine folder.
impact.L2: A full disk stops being the reason for slow or failing software at the office.
impact.L3: A routine cleanup is one approved step that records how much was moved.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.

levers.name: device.restart-service
levers.description: Restart one service from the approved list (Dnscache, W32Time, BITS, wuauserv, LanmanWorkstation) on one device, using the vetted script dev-service-restart. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

service.description: Service name from the approved list

impact.L1: A stuck name lookup, clock or update service on that device works again without a reboot.
impact.L2: The office avoids a restart in the middle of the day for a problem one service caused.
impact.L3: Only five named services can be restarted; anything else is not a lever.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.

levers.name: device.reboot
levers.description: Restart one workstation or laptop of the client, using the vetted script dev-reboot-workstation. A server is refused. The runner's business-hours window rule applies. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

impact.L1: The person's machine restarts; unsaved work in open programs is lost, so they are told first.
impact.L2: A frozen or half-updated workstation is fixed with one approved restart at a time the client's window allows.
impact.L3: Restarts are rationed per client per hour, so a mistake cannot restart a whole office.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.

levers.name: device.reboot-server
levers.description: Restart one server of the client, using the vetted script dev-reboot-server. A workstation is refused. The runner's maintenance-window rule applies. Mock RMM only.

device.description: RMM device uid of one device of the client (from the device list), for example c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000d0001

impact.L1: Everyone using that server's files or applications loses their connection while it restarts.
impact.L2: A server restart happens only in the maintenance window on the client's record, never by default.
impact.L3: Server restarts are the tightest capped lever in the family: two per client per hour.
impact.L4: Same-client device only; another client's device answers like an absent one, and the script cannot be changed by the caller.
